cards.meaning: With distrust or a habit of expecting the worst.
cards.example: The board viewed another price rise with a jaundiced eye.

cards.meaning: Choose a position between two extremes.
cards.example: The PTA tried to steer a middle course on school fees.

cards.front: with their tails between their legs
cards.meaning: Showing shame after a defeat or mistake.
cards.example: Our team left the pitch with their tails between their legs.

cards.meaning: Taken a decisive step that cannot easily be reversed.
cards.example: When the cooperative signed the lease, it had crossed the Rubicon.

cards.meaning: Too impressed by his own importance or abilities.
cards.example: The new captain sounded full of himself at assembly.

cards.meaning: Stopped helping her when she still needed help.
cards.example: When Bisi's partner quit before the school debate, he left her in the lurch.

cards.meaning: Using his position or power to boss people around.
cards.example: The prefect was throwing his weight about in the canteen queue.

cards.front: between a rock and a hard place
cards.meaning: Facing two choices that both have serious drawbacks.
cards.example: With both suppliers raising prices, the trader was between a rock and a hard place.

cards.meaning: Avoid a duty or get out of trouble by talking persuasively.
cards.example: Bola tried to talk his way out of tidying the classroom.

cards.meaning: In words that make a strong opinion completely clear.
cards.example: The principal rejected the proposal in no uncertain terms.

cards.meaning: Start organising himself well enough to succeed.
cards.example: Musa had to get his act together before the Kano debate.

cards.meaning: Stay calm and stop being impatient or angry.
cards.example: Tomi told her sister to keep her shirt on while they waited for a danfo.

cards.meaning: Spend nearly all one's time together.
cards.example: The twins live in each other's pockets at boarding school.

cards.meaning: Feel very excited for something to happen soon.
cards.example: I can't wait to see the Eagles play in Uyo.

cards.meaning: A knack for spotting a good story.
cards.example: The school reporter has a nose for stories about local sports.

cards.meaning: If the cost were taken out of consideration.
cards.example: But for the expense, our class would travel to Abuja by air.

cards.front: At the turn of the century
cards.meaning: Around the time one century ends and the next begins.
cards.example: The class read about life in Lagos at the turn of the century.

cards.meaning: Very close to a new or dangerous situation.
cards.example: The Abuja team was on the brink of elimination.

cards.meaning: Objected to something because it seemed wrong or offensive.
cards.example: The prefect took exception to the joke made at assembly.

cards.meaning: Cannot act because something prevents it.
cards.example: The prefect said her hands are tied until the head teacher returns.

cards.meaning: Leave an old problem alone so it does not start up again.
cards.example: The prefect chose to let the sleeping dog lie after the quarrel ended.

cards.meaning: Have enough money to cover basic expenses.
cards.example: The Lagos trader took extra work to make both ends meet.

cards.meaning: At a distance that keeps someone from getting too close to you.
cards.example: After the quarrel, Ngozi kept her neighbour at arm's length.

cards.front: a chip off the old block
cards.meaning: Someone whose character or habits strongly resemble a parent's.
cards.example: Aba traders say the young tailor is a chip off the old block.

cards.meaning: Try to win a crowd's approval through showy words or actions.
cards.example: The debate coach told Sade not to play to the gallery.

cards.meaning: A state of happiness based on false hopes.
cards.example: The side lived in a fool's paradise until the first league match.

cards.meaning: A tiny amount compared with what is needed.
cards.example: One bag of cement was a drop in the ocean for the school repairs.

cards.meaning: Being planned or prepared.
cards.example: A borehole is in the pipeline for the village school.

cards.meaning: Something is so unlikely that it will probably never happen.
cards.example: Ada joked that pigs would fly before her brother washed the danfo.

cards.meaning: Suddenly surprised or unsettled.
cards.example: Ngozi was taken aback when they called her name at assembly.

cards.meaning: A difficult time with a number of setbacks.
cards.example: The team had a bumpy ride through the city league.

cards.front: take my eyes off the ball
cards.meaning: Stop paying attention to what matters most.
cards.example: I took my eyes off the ball and missed the final question in the school debate.

cards.meaning: With only enough money or supplies for immediate needs.
cards.example: A loss of stock left the trader living hand-to-mouth.

cards.meaning: Stop believing you can succeed and feel discouraged.
cards.example: Do not lose heart if you miss a question in the mock exam.

cards.meaning: A hidden weakness in a person who seems admirable.
cards.example: The captain showed feet of clay when he blamed a junior player for his mistake.

cards.meaning: An unusually good chance to do something.
cards.example: The Lagos science fair was a golden opportunity to show our work.

cards.front: a taste of their own medicine
cards.meaning: The same unpleasant treatment they gave to someone else.
cards.example: The boys got a taste of their own medicine when their classmates hid their football.

cards.meaning: A view of a place from high above it.
cards.example: We had a bird’s-eye view of the market from the footbridge.

cards.meaning: Suffered a setback, loss or damage.
cards.example: The Kano stall took a hit after the road closed.

cards.meaning: No more than the amount named.
cards.example: The walk to the Enugu market takes ten minutes at the most.
